In nineteen ninety, Voyager 1 was leaving home forever.
Before it went, Carl Sagan asked for one favour: turn around, and take a picture of us.
It did. The whole Earth was smaller than one pixel.
Thirty-four minutes later, they switched its cameras off. It never saw home again.
It's still out there. So far away now, a hello takes a whole day to reach it.
